action.question: Where should the new stage env live?

questions.question: Where should the new stage env live?

options.label: Same host (spirit), separate stack
options.description: New compose project on spirit with different ports/container names; cheapest, but a spirit-level compromise still hits both.

options.label: Different host entirely
options.description: Stage on another machine (e.g., a separate VM or your Mac mini). True blast-radius isolation, but more infra to set up.

options.label: Cloud VM (AWS/Hetzner/etc.)
options.description: Most isolated and closest to a real decom story (prod just disappears), but biggest cost/setup lift.

questions.question: What DB does stage start from?

options.label: Latest prod dump, AS-IS (real data)
options.description: Maximum fidelity for the parallel-run test. Stage holds real PII — same protection level as prod required.

options.label: Prod dump anonymized via prod_to_dev.sql
options.description: Lower exposure if stage creds leak. But you're then NOT testing on prod-equivalent data, which weakens the parallel-run signal.

options.label: Fresh DB, replay-from-prod later
options.description: Stage runs empty until cutover day; replay/dump-restore happens at swap time. Cleaner secrets boundary but less parallel-run value.

questions.question: What's the gate for "100% working" before cutover?

options.label: Full nightly test suite green on stage + manual smoke
options.description: Tight, objective. Doesn't catch real-user usage gaps.

options.label: N days of parallel use, both envs writable
options.description: Catches usage gaps, but you now have two divergent DBs to reconcile at cutover. Hardest.

options.label: N days parallel, stage read-only-mirror of prod
options.description: Stage replays prod, users still write to prod. No reconciliation; clean swap when ready. Recommended.

options.label: Decide later in the plan doc
options.description: Defer this; I'll just sketch the structure and you fill in the criteria as it firms up.

questions.question: What do you want me to do right now?

options.label: Draft a new master tracker comment on #36
options.description: Edit #36 to reflect the new plan, mark #20/#34 as superseded, open a placeholder for the stage-build epic. Minimal commits.

options.label: Open a new epic ticket + close superseded ones
options.description: File a fresh "stage-mirror-then-decom-prod" epic, link from #36, close/won't-do #20 #34. Cleaner board, more churn.

options.label: Just sketch the plan in this chat
options.description: No ticket edits yet; we iterate here first, then I update the board once shape is clear.

## Bottom line
You're one human-only gate away: **#20's prod APP_KEY check on `spirit`**. Once that's signed off, #10 (the flip) and #11 (re-enable scanning) are the last two clicks. Everything an agent can do has already landed.

I want to change the plan to duplicate the prod env as stage but all things like prod (duplicate db and etc).
We should bring stage to 100% working, run them in parallel, than decomm prod

That's a significantly safer cutover — no in-place secret rotation on prod, and you get to test the full stack on a real prod-equivalent DB before flipping users.

The plan change collapses several open tickets:
- **#20** "Prod APP_KEY check + rotate-if-match" → moot. Fresh stage gets fresh secrets; old prod APP_KEY just dies with the host.
- **#34** "PROD bulk password reset" → moot for the same reason; the leaked-key concern is decommissioned, not patched.
- **#10** "make repo public" — unblocked sooner; stage doesn't need to exist before the flip (the repo audit was the actual gate, not the prod rotation).

What this **adds** as new work (no ticket today):
1. Stand up `stage` on a separate host (or separate compose stack on `spirit`?) mirroring prod's Dockerfile/compose
2. Restore latest prod DB dump → stage DB (with or without anonymization? prod-equivalent suggests **with** real data, behind auth)
3. Fresh `.env.stage` (new APP_KEY, new DB pw, vaulted via SOPS) committed as `.env.stage.sops`
4. Parallel-run window: define what "100% working" means (smoke test? full Dusk? user-driven acceptance for N days?)
5. Cutover: DNS/port swap or hostname swap; freeze writes on old prod during the swap
6. Decom plan: prod-down checklist, retain DB snapshot, revoke creds, archive container
